subject.title: feat(acp): pipe lifeline — reap the bridge tree on abrupt owner death

question: Should acpx adopt a lazily compiled native POSIX lifeline and detached bridge process groups as the default core solution for abrupt owner-death cleanup?
rationale: The patch appears technically sound, but it establishes new native compilation, executable cache, environment override, packaging, signal, and process-group conventions that repository policy says require deliberate long-term product scrutiny.

options.title: Adopt after rebase
options.body: Accept the native lifeline as core behavior, rebase the branch, and require fresh Linux and macOS lifecycle and packaging proof on the exact head.

options.title: Narrow to cooperative cleanup
options.body: Land only group-aware normal-close and startup-failure cleanup while deferring abrupt owner-death handling until a different cross-platform lifecycle design is approved.

options.title: Decline native core surface
options.body: Keep current process semantics and close the PR if acpx should not compile, cache, or execute a native helper at runtime.

recommendation.title: Adopt after rebase
recommendation.body: Accept the native lifeline as core behavior, rebase the branch, and require fresh Linux and macOS lifecycle and packaging proof on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged queue-owner lifecycle work makes this the strongest available owner for the adjacent process-lifecycle and operational-contract decision.
